# Information on How These Data Are Organized:

`Trial` indicates the trial number that participants are on. -12 to -1 are the 12 practice trials. There were 250 trials in the experiment. The first 50 trials, participants could respond at their leisure. After that, we applied a threshold for their RT: the 60th percentile of their repeat trials. Participants were told that their responses would now need to be quick *and* accurate. A new threshold was applied again after 100 trials. Please see our manuscript / registration at https://osf.io/7jfbp/ for more details.

`Task` refers to the specific task judgement: judging whether a letter is a vowel or consonant or whether it is printed in uppercase or lowercase.

`TaskColor` refers to the color of the border that indicates the specific task judgement. This is because we have counterbalanced for assignment of the task color judgements to specific tasks across different task versions. (We also counterbalance for the predictive identity of the subliminal/supraliminal cues).

`Continuity` indicates the trial type: a task-repeat or task-switch. Notably, in this task, the overall task context is a 75:25 repeat:switch context.

`StimLetter` refers to the stimulus to which the participant responded on each trial.

`StimLetterStartTime` & `StimLetterEndTime` document the time at which the stimulus was on the screen. This is important for our task because of the different RT thresholds. Note that in the beginning, RT is just the difference between these two, and there are likely outliers in the RTs. However, after the 50th trial (trial 49), the threshold has been applied, and the RTs become narrower in their distribution.

`Response` indicates what the participant responded & `CorrectAnswer` indicates what they should have pressed. When `Response` == `CorrectAnswer` (within the threshold that is in place at the time of the particular trial), `Accuracy` = 1; Else `Accuracy` = 0.

`RT` is recorded in seconds. Here it is simply calculated as the EndTime - StartTime of the stimuli, because the stimulus was removed from the screen as soon as a participant responded or the RT threshold deadline was applied (i.e., lack of response before threshold deadline met). (In the code, it's specified as a timer to zero when the stimulus appears and if a response button is pressed, the timer ends; note RT cells are blank when there is no response.)

`fixationStartTimeinOverallExp` is a global clock, so it records how long it's been since the experiment began (since the fixation is the start of the trial, this column essentially gives how long into the experiment this trial is beginning) & `fixationStartTime`  is 0 because that's when the trial begins; it's just really a manipulation check as much as anything & `fixationEndTime` marks the end of the fixation period.

`CueStartTime` is when the subliminal (Expts 1/2) and supraliminal (Expts 3/4) cue was shown on screen and `CueEndTime` is when the cue was removed from the screen. The cue was displayed for 11.67 ms (aka 1 screen refresh), so it was important to make sure that the timing was consistent across most trials.

`Cue` could be 2, 4, or 8. One of the cues was 100% predictive of switch trials, one was 100% predictive of repeat trials, one was nonpredictive (i.e., preceded trials at the same percentage as the overall task context).

`MaskStartTime` & `MaskEndTime` likewise mark the onset and removal of the mask that made the cue subliminal in Expts 1/2. This lasted 494 ms.

`Session` refers to the Experiment number in the study. Experiment 2 is the same as Experiment 1, but with additional task instructions meant to inform participants of the predictive value of the cues. Experiment 3 is the same as Experiment 1, but with the cues made supraliminal. Experiment 4 has the instructions of Experiment 2 and supraliminal cues like Experiment 3.

`Participant` - self-explanatory.

`CueVersion` refers to the task version. As I noted earlier, we counterbalanced across task-color/task judgement and cue identity (e.g., whether 2 was predictive of switch or repeats, or not predictive at all) assignments.

In CueVersion 0 and 1, the predictive switch is 2
In CueVersion 2 and 3, the predictive switch is 4
In CueVersion 4 and 5, the predictive switch is 8

In CueVersion 3 and 5, the predictive repeat is 2
In CueVersion 1 and 4, the predictive repeat is 4
In CueVersion 0 and 2, the predictive repeat is 8

In CueVersion 2 and 4, the non-predictive cue is 2
In CueVersion 0 and 5, the non-predictive cue is 4
In CueVersion 1 and 3, the non-predictive cue is 8

`FrameRate` refers to the frame rate on our CRT monitor.

`ExpName` refers to the name of the experiment script.

`CueType` refers to whether the cue was predictive or nonpredictive. We coded this based on CueVersion in the other experiments, and this data is now filtered for that purpose.

# Rather than do cleaning on the experiment csv files, we've compiled the filtered csv files.

This is because one of the RT filters is if RT is +3 SDs, and if I did this with the compiled csv file and then filtered before data analysis, that would shift the filter values differently than if I'd filtered within experiment and then compiled the files for data analysis. The latter approach is more close to what we're actually trying to conclude with an across experiment analysis.

Note that this particular script is for the Supplementary text, in which we include participants who were excluded from the main data analysis. This means that the Experiments will have different N (E1, 47; E2, 56; E3, 48; E4, 50).

*after loading in required packages (not shown here in HTML)...*

```{r setup}
#import raw data
data.accanaly <- read.csv("AllExpts_AllSubs_RegData_ACC.csv", header=T,na.strings=c(""))
data.accanaly$Accuracy <- as.numeric(as.character(data.accanaly$Accuracy))
data.accanaly$TrialType <- data.accanaly$Continuity
data.accanaly$sub <- data.accanaly$participant
data.accanaly$expt <- data.accanaly$session

data.rtanaly <- read.csv("AllExpts_AllSubs_RegData_RT.csv", header=T,na.strings=c(""))
data.rtanaly$RT <- as.numeric(as.character(data.rtanaly$RT))
data.rtanaly$Accuracy <- as.numeric(as.character(data.rtanaly$Accuracy))
data.rtanaly$TrialType <- data.rtanaly$Continuity
data.rtanaly$sub <- data.rtanaly$participant
data.rtanaly$expt <- data.rtanaly$session

#Creating the Preparatory Cue Knowledge variable (implicit/explicit) + the awareness (subliminal/supraliminal) variable
data.rtanaly <- mutate(data.rtanaly, CueKnowledge = case_when(expt %in% c(1,3) ~ 'A: Non-Explicit', TRUE ~ 'B: Explicit'))
data.accanaly <- mutate(data.accanaly, CueKnowledge = case_when(expt %in% c(1,3) ~ 'non-explicit', TRUE ~ 'explicit'))

data.rtanaly <- mutate(data.rtanaly, CueAware = case_when(expt %in% c(1,2) ~ 'subliminal', TRUE ~ 'supraliminal'))
data.accanaly <- mutate(data.accanaly, CueAware = case_when(expt %in% c(1,2) ~ 'subliminal', TRUE ~ 'supraliminal'))

data.rtanaly <- mutate(data.rtanaly, ExptName = case_when(expt %in% c(1) ~ '1: subliminal, non-explicit', expt %in% c(2) ~ '2: subliminal, explicit', expt %in% c(3) ~ '3: supraliminal, non-explicit', TRUE ~ '4: supraliminal, explicit'))
data.accanaly <- mutate(data.accanaly, ExptName = case_when(expt %in% c(1) ~ '1: subliminal, non-explicit', expt %in% c(2) ~ '2: subliminal, explicit', expt %in% c(3) ~ '3: supraliminal, non-explicit', TRUE ~ '4: supraliminal, explicit'))

```

# What are our conditions for data analysis?

From our Stage 1 preregistered manuscript (https://osf.io/tnzvb/):

Median reaction time (RT) data will be analyzed for correct trials in which participants were not excessively slow (<200 ms) or fast (+3 SDs) to respond. We will also analyze accuracy data, and divide RT by accuracy data to obtain a global performance index, consistent with Farooqui and Manly (2015).

Note that for within-experiment comparisons, median RT, instead of mean RT, will be used to facilitate an optimal comparison with Farooqui and Manly (2015). However, because sequential Bayes Factor analysis may lead to uneven sample sizes between experiments and because small sample sizes overestimate the true median (Miller, 1998), we will use mean RT to compare effects between experiments.

We will run a repeated-measures ANOVA with cue (predictive/non-predictive) and trial type (task-switch/task-repeat) as within-subjects factors. We expect to find an interaction between cue and trial type, such that participants are quicker and more efficient to respond to task-switch trials following the predictive vs. non-predictive cues.

Because our experiments involve a 2x2 design with independent manipulations of conscious perception and knowledge, we will combine the data across experiments and run a Bayesian repeated-measures ANOVA that includes cue visibility (subliminal/supraliminal) and preparatory cue knowledge (implicit/explicit) as between-subjects factors, in addition to our within-subjects factors of cue (predictive/non-predictive) and trial type (task-switch/task-repeat). This will quantify the amount of evidence that conscious perception and knowledge impact control-learning. 

We will also run equivalence tests using the two one-sided test procedure, in order to provide support for the potential lack of a meaningful effect. This could occur in individual experiment manipulations or when we compare effects between experiments.

#### Aggregate the data for analysis, create Global Performance Index metric

```{r data aggregate}
st.err <- function(x) {
    sd(x)/sqrt(length(x))
}

#reaction time
data.anova.rt <- data.rtanaly %>% group_by(sub, TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge, CueAware) %>% summarise(RT = mean(RT))

#accuracy
data.anova.acc <- data.accanaly %>% group_by(sub, TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge, CueAware) %>% summarise(Accuracy = mean(Accuracy))

#global performance index
data.ie = data.frame(IE=(((data.anova.acc$Accuracy*100)/data.anova.rt$RT)*100), TrialType=data.anova.acc$TrialType, CueType=data.anova.acc$CueType, sub=data.anova.acc$sub, CueKnowledge = data.anova.acc$CueKnowledge, CueAware = data.anova.acc$CueAware)

write.csv(data.anova.rt, file="AllExpts_ANOVA_RT_supp.csv")
write.csv(data.anova.acc, file="AllExpts_ANOVA_ACC_supp.csv")
write.csv(data.ie, file="AllExpts_ANOVA_IE_supp.csv")

```

#### Run repeated-measures ANOVAs on RT, accuracy, and Global Performance Index

```{r rm ANOVAs}

RTanova <- aov_car(RT ~ CueKnowledge * CueAware + Error(sub/(CueType*TrialType)), data = data.anova.rt, anova_table = list(es = "pes"))
RTanova

#three-decimal p in accordance w/ APA guidelines
print_anova(RTanova, decimals_p = 3)

ACCanova <- aov_car(Accuracy ~ CueKnowledge * CueAware + Error(sub/(CueType*TrialType)), data = data.anova.acc, anova_table = list(es = "pes"))
ACCanova

#three-decimal p in accordance w/ APA guidelines
print_anova(ACCanova, decimals_p = 3)

IEanova <- aov_car(IE ~ CueKnowledge * CueAware + Error(sub/(CueType*TrialType)), data = data.ie, anova_table = list(es = "pes"))
IEanova

#three-decimal p in accordance w/ APA guidelines
print_anova(IEanova, decimals_p = 3)

```

```{r prep across expt graph, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
#### Prepare dataframes for Plotting
#reaction time
data.anova.rt.e <- data.rtanaly %>% group_by(sub, TrialType, CueType, ExptName) %>% summarise(RT = mean(RT))

#accuracy
data.anova.acc.e <- data.accanaly %>% group_by(sub, TrialType, CueType, ExptName) %>% summarise(Accuracy = mean(Accuracy))

#global performance index
data.ie.e = data.frame(IE=(((data.anova.acc.e$Accuracy*100)/data.anova.rt.e$RT)*100), TrialType=data.anova.acc.e$TrialType, CueType=data.anova.acc.e$CueType, sub=data.anova.acc.e$sub, ExptName = data.anova.acc.e$ExptName)

#calculate switch costs within the dataframe for data.anova.rt
setDT(data.anova.rt.e)
setkey(data.anova.rt.e, TrialType)
diffscore.rt <- data.anova.rt.e[ , diff := c(NA, diff(RT)), by = list(sub, CueType, ExptName)]  

setDT(data.ie.e)
setkey(data.ie.e, TrialType)
diffscore.ie <- data.ie.e[ , diff := c(NA, diff(IE)), by = list(sub, CueType, ExptName)]

setDT(data.anova.rt)
setkey(data.anova.rt, TrialType)
diffscore.sc <- data.anova.rt[ , diff := c(NA, diff(RT)), by = list(sub, CueType, CueKnowledge, CueAware)]

#it put the switch costs into the rows with "switch as a trial, so remove repeat as a trial type"
switch.rt <- data.anova.rt.e[with (data.anova.rt.e, TrialType != "repeat"),]
switch.ie <- data.ie.e[with (data.ie.e, TrialType != "repeat"),]
switch.sc <- data.anova.rt[with (data.anova.rt, TrialType != "repeat"),]

#get rid of TrialType + RT/IE as columns now
switch.rt = subset(switch.rt, select = c(CueType,ExptName,sub,diff))
switch.ie = subset(switch.ie, select = c(CueType,ExptName,sub,diff))
switch.sc = subset(switch.sc, select = c(sub,CueType,CueKnowledge,CueAware,diff))

#rename column to reflect switch cost
switch.rt$switchcost <- switch.rt$diff
switch.ie$switchcost <- switch.ie$diff
switch.sc$switchcost <- switch.sc$diff

#means for the plots
switch.plot.rt <- switch.rt %>% group_by(CueType, ExptName) %>% summarise(RT = mean(switchcost))
switch.plot.ie <- switch.ie %>% group_by(CueType, ExptName) %>% summarise(IE = mean(switchcost))
switch.plot.sc <- switch.sc %>% group_by(CueKnowledge, CueAware, CueType) %>% summarise(SC = mean(switchcost))

#standard error of the mean
switch.rt.se <- switch.rt %>% group_by(CueType, ExptName) %>% summarise(RT.se = st.err(switchcost))
switch.ie.se <- switch.ie %>% group_by(CueType, ExptName) %>% summarise(IE.se = st.err(switchcost))
switch.sc.se <- switch.sc %>% group_by(CueKnowledge, CueAware, CueType) %>% summarise(SC.se = st.err(switchcost))

```

```{r prep the graphs, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

#many plots - subliminal v. supraliminal, explicit vs. implicit (averaged across expts); breaking down further is the same as the expt plots in the other scripts

#reaction time
data.plot.rt.ck <- data.rtanaly %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge) %>% summarise(RT = mean(RT))
data.se.rt.ck <- data.anova.rt %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge) %>% summarise(RT.se = st.err(RT))

data.plot.rt.ca <- data.rtanaly %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueAware) %>% summarise(RT = mean(RT))
data.se.rt.ca <- data.anova.rt %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueAware) %>% summarise(RT.se = st.err(RT))

#accuracy
data.plot.acc.ck <- data.accanaly %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge) %>% summarise(Accuracy = mean(Accuracy))
data.se.acc.ck <- data.anova.acc %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge) %>% summarise(Accuracy.se = st.err(Accuracy))

data.plot.acc.ca <- data.accanaly %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueAware) %>% summarise(Accuracy = mean(Accuracy))
data.se.acc.ca <- data.anova.acc %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueAware) %>% summarise(Accuracy.se = st.err(Accuracy))

#global performance index
data.plot.ie.ck <- data.ie %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge) %>% summarise(IE = mean(IE))
data.se.ie.ck <- data.ie %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueKnowledge) %>% summarise(IE.se = st.err(IE))

data.plot.ie.ca <- data.ie %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueAware) %>% summarise(IE = mean(IE))
data.se.ie.ca <- data.ie %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType, CueAware) %>% summarise(IE.se = st.err(IE))
```

### Plot the Results

#### Across Experiment Switch Costs - RT (Supplemental)

```{r fig 2, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}

ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data=switch.plot.sc, aes(x = factor(CueAware), y = (SC), fill = factor(CueType)), position = "dodge", stat = "identity", width = 0.75)  + 
    geom_point(data = switch.sc, aes(x =factor(CueAware), y = (switchcost), color = factor(CueType)), position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width=0.2, dodge.width = .75), alpha = 1/2, size=3, show.legend=FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("gray74", "gray74"), name= "Cue Type") +
  geom_errorbar(data=switch.plot.sc, aes(x=(factor(switch.plot.sc$CueAware)), ymin=(switch.plot.sc$SC-switch.sc.se$SC.se), ymax=(switch.plot.sc$SC+switch.sc.se$SC.se), fill = factor(CueType)), stat="identity", width=0, size=2,position=position_dodge(.75), inherit.aes = TRUE) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-100,500)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9"), name= "Cue Type") +
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Cue Visibility", labels=c("Subliminal", "Supraliminal")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(-100, 500, 100)) +
  labs(title= ("Switch Costs across Experiments"), y="Mean Response Time (ms)")  +
  theme_classic(base_size = 26) +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 26, family = "Myriad Pro")) +
  facet_wrap(~CueKnowledge) +
      NULL

ggsave("Supplemental_RTSwitchCosts.pdf", plot=last_plot(), dpi=300, width=11, height=8)

```

```{r, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 8}
    theme(text = element_text(size = 26, family = "Myriad Pro")) +
    NULL

p + facet_wrap(~ CueAware)

ggsave("AllExpt_meanacc_ca_supp.pdf", plot=last_plot(), dpi=300, width=11, height=8)

```

#### What about Bayesian ANOVAs? Printed below are the inclusion BFs.

What are inclusion Bayes Factors? From https://easystats.github.io/bayestestR/articles/bayes_factors.html:

"Inclusion Bayes factors answer the question:

Are the observed data more probable under models with a particular predictor, than they are under models without that particular predictor?

In other words, on average - are models with predictor X more likely to have produce the observed data than models without predictor X?

Since each model has a prior probability, it is possible to sum the prior probability of all models that include a predictor of interest (the prior inclusion probability), and of all models that do not include that predictor (the prior exclusion probability). After the data are observed, we can similarly consider the sums of the posterior models' probabilities to obtain the posterior inclusion probability and the posterior exclusion probability. Again, the change from prior to posterior inclusion odds is the Inclusion Bayes factor ("BFInclusion"; Clyde, Ghosh, & Littman, 2011)."

The first model will refer to RT.

```{r RT bayes anova, echo=FALSE}

data.anova.rt <- data.frame(data.anova.rt)

#factorizing the data to run the ANOVAs
data.anova.rt <- within(data.anova.rt, {TrialType <- factor(TrialType)
  sub <- factor(sub)
  CueType <- factor(CueType)
  CueKnowledge <- factor(CueKnowledge)
  CueAware <- factor(CueAware)
})

#inclusionBF + anovaBF
bf_rt <- anovaBF(RT ~ CueType * TrialType * CueKnowledge * CueAware + sub, data = data.anova.rt, 
             whichRandom="sub")

print(inclusionBF(bf_rt))

```

The second model refers to accuracy.

```{r ACC bayes anova, echo=FALSE}

data.anova.acc <- data.frame(data.anova.acc)

data.anova.acc <- within(data.anova.acc, {TrialType <- factor(TrialType) 
sub <- factor(sub) 
CueType <- factor(CueType)
CueKnowledge <- factor(CueKnowledge)
  CueAware <- factor(CueAware)
})

bf_acc <- anovaBF(Accuracy ~ CueType * TrialType * CueKnowledge * CueAware + sub, data = data.anova.acc, 
             whichRandom="sub")

print(inclusionBF(bf_acc))

```

The final model refers to the global performance index.

```{r bayes anova, echo=FALSE}

data.ie <- within(data.ie, {TrialType <- factor(TrialType) 
sub <- factor(sub) 
CueType <- factor(CueType)
CueKnowledge <- factor(CueKnowledge)
  CueAware <- factor(CueAware)
})

bf_ie <- anovaBF(IE ~ CueType * TrialType * CueKnowledge * CueAware + sub, data = data.ie, 
             whichRandom="sub")

print(inclusionBF(bf_ie))

```

Visualizing the Bayes Factor Anovas with plot(bf_rt) etc. does not help in this case because with four factors (Cue Type, Trial Type, Cue Knowledge, Cue Aware), there are too many models to visualize.

# Supplementary Tables

These tables below are averaging across all the experiments. Each individual Experiment script has the median RT/mean ACC/median index + 95% confidence interval. The following tables would be if the cue knowledge or awareness variables did not matter (although we've seen that they do in the bar graphs above).

#### Supplementary Table for Global Performance Index

```{r table index,echo=FALSE}

data.se.ie <- data.ie %>% group_by(TrialType, CueType) %>% summarise(IE.se = st.err(IE))
```
